clue.text: Member brought to order in the end is recipient of leg-up

indicators.note: in tells us the pair of short pieces sits inside the word for the end

parts.note: the end is the last
MP is a Member of Parliament
PO is a postal order

explanation.surface: A parliamentarian called to order finally gets a helping hand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg-up' suggests a boost, but here it is a dog lifting its leg against a street light.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs famously cock a leg against a street light standard, so it receives the lifted leg.

clue.text: Number getting whip-round which is generous

indicators.note: round means the whip goes round the number

parts.note: lash means whip
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A number getting a whip-round shows generosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' looks like a collection of money, but it splits: the whip goes round the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish means giving or spending freely, openhanded.

clue.text: Poet has same problem with remaining runners

indicators.note: problem signals the word same is knotted into a new order

parts.note: the field is all the runners left in a race

explanation.surface: A poet shares the trouble of the horses still running.
explanation.walkthrough: John Masefield was a British Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: John Masefield, author of 'Sea-Fever', was a British Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Money, in a word, for trying to catch prisoner-simpler to go without

indicators.note: to go without means the simpler word goes outside the other pieces

parts.note: purer means simpler, less mixed
chasing is trying to catch
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: Money is needed to try to catch a prisoner, with simpler folk left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Money is in effect the ability to buy; that buying capacity is its economic meaning in a word.

clue.text: Bird and beast about to pull up

indicators.note: about tells us the beast goes round the other piece

parts.note: a seal is a beast

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word for pull is read upwards

parts.note: to lug is to pull

explanation.surface: A bird and a beast pull up together.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull of the coast is a seabird.

clue.text: Follower of Lloyd who uses the internet?

explanation.surface: A disciple of Lloyd is apparently someone who browses online.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Lloyd Webber is the composer whose surname follows Lloyd; jokingly, a web user would be a 'web-er'.

clue.text: First drink served to general in army

indicators.note: served signals the letters of to general in army are dished up in a new order

explanation.surface: A general in the army is brought his first cup of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' looks like waiting at table but signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa brought to bed at dawn is the day's first drink.

clue.text: Put up with stream

explanation.surface: Tolerate a flowing creek.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate it; a brook is also a small creek.

clue.text: Satyrs with curls

explanation.surface: Mythical goat-men with curly locks.
explanation.walkthrough: Satyrs here are butterflies, not mythical beings: ringlets belong to the satyr butterfly group.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs are a group of brown butterflies including the ringlet; ringlets are also long spiral curls of hair.

clue.text: Witness witnessing cricket?

explanation.surface: Someone who saw a cricket match testifies.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; someone watching is 'at Test'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness is to certify; jokingly, someone watching a Test match is 'at Test'.

clue.text: Caller drops it to protect the face

indicators.note: drops means the caller loses the little word it from inside

parts.note: a caller is a visitor

explanation.surface: A visitor lets something fall to shield their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes IT from VISITOR. The definition 'to protect the face' describes the object's job; read it as 'thing to protect the face'.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet's movable front piece or a cap's peak shields the face and eyes.

clue.text: Initially the prime minister's time

parts.note: the initials of prime minister are P and M, which also stand for post meridiem, the hours after midday

explanation.surface: A remark about the first period of a premier's tenure.
explanation.definitionFit: P.M. (post meridiem) labels the hours after midday, the same letters as a prime minister's initials.

clue.text: Refuge for Peter at Cambridge college?

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a house is a college, as in Peterhouse at Cambridge

explanation.surface: Somewhere for Peter to shelter at his Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterhouse is the oldest Cambridge college; swap its 'Peter' for the safecracker's sense, a safe, and keep 'house'.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret dwelling where people can hide from enemies or pursuers is a sanctuary.

clue.text: Hick laying burden on student

parts.note: a yoke is a heavy burden
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin piles a load onto a learner.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'laying ... on' puts the burden first and the student after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic, unsophisticated countryman is a bumpkin.

clue.text: Musteline words

parts.note: musteline means of the stoat family, and evasive talk is named after one such animal

explanation.surface: Words of the weasel family, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: The stoat family's small slender hunter gives its name to evasive 'weasel words'.

clue.text: Consideration needed even if at heart of match

parts.note: even if means though

indicators.note: at heart of picks the central letter of the word match

explanation.surface: Care is needed even when the match hangs in the balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful reflection or deliberation is mental consideration.

clue.text: Setting of relegation?

explanation.surface: Where demotion takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun that is setting is sinking below the horizon; a relegated club drops a division.

clue.text: It's sweet to spend some time with girls

parts.note: a mo is a moment, some time
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: It's lovely to pass a while with young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle-like dark syrup from sugar refining is a sweetener.

clue.text: Say the first row to get talked about

indicators.note: about means the spoken word goes around the noise

parts.note: talked means oral, spoken
a row is a din, a racket

explanation.surface: Announce the front row so it gets discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a line of seats but is a noisy din; 'first' is an example of a number word giving position.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as first, second and third, giving position in a series, are this kind of number.

clue.text: River's existence cut short by clairvoyant

definitions.note: the possessive reads as river is

indicators.note: cut short means the word for existence loses its last letter

parts.note: life is existence
fey means having second sight

explanation.surface: A river's life was ended early by a psychic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liffey is the river through Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin's main waterway is an Irish river.

clue.text: The man to note to thing — it's a plant

parts.note: he is the man
NB, nota bene, means note well
it is a thing

explanation.surface: A botanical riddle built word by word from a man, a note and a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-nettle relative, a common weed of gardens and fields, is a plant.

clue.text: Castle town has its prince topped and tailed before church

indicators.note: topped and tailed means the prince's name loses first and last letters

parts.note: Charles was the Prince of Wales

explanation.surface: A castle town has its prince beheaded and docked before church.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlech is a Welsh town with a famous castle, fitting a Prince of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlech in Wales is known for its thirteenth-century fortress.

clue.text: Schoenberg's music is not a la mode

definitions.note: an adjective describing music; read as music that is keyless

indicators.note: mode signals a rearranged fashion of the letters of not a la

explanation.surface: Schoenberg's music is unfashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a la mode' looks like 'in fashion'; 'mode' alone is the anagram signal on NOT A LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoenberg's twelve-tone music abandons any key or tonal centre.

clue.text: Ancient writer, the first to sit back

parts.note: A is first, as in A1

indicators.note: back means the word for sitting for a portrait is read the other way

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: An old author is the first to sit at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek fabulist of the sixth century BC is a classical author.

clue.text: Boy says he'll play ball after suggested start

definitions.text: Boy says he'll play ball after suggested start

parts.words: Boy says he'll play ball after suggested start
parts.note: the children's game in which players obey only orders opening with a certain boy's name and says

explanation.surface: A boy promises to cooperate once a start is suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: In the party game, players obey an order only if it starts with this name plus 'says'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the children's party game, a command counts only when it opens with this boy's name followed by 'says'.

clue.text: Time for the intoxicated to conceal name

indicators.note: to conceal means the drunk word hides the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: tight means drunk

explanation.surface: Drunks need time to hide their identity.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of two weeks is a span of time.

clue.text: Annoyed about catcall he made in unspecified locality

indicators.note: about places the annoyed word around the cry and the pronoun

parts.note: sore means annoyed
a mew is a cat's call
taken as written

explanation.surface: An irritated man let out a jeer in some place or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catcall' looks like a jeer but is literally a cat's call, a mew.
explanation.definitionFit: An indefinite, unnamed place is some location or other.

clue.text: Point to its conclusion on the blower

definitions.text: Point to its conclusion on the blower

indicators.note: to its conclusion picks the final letter of the word point

parts.note: a horn is something you blow

explanation.surface: Someone points to the end of a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the blower' is British slang for the telephone, a red herring; here it is a horn. 'on' places the final letter of 'Point' before HORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp spine on a rose stem is a pointed spike.

clue.text: Guard Southgate?

parts.note: split the place name as south plus gate: S for south and an entry for a gate give a watchman

explanation.surface: A football manager called Southgate keeping guard.
explanation.walkthrough: Gareth Southgate is an English footballer and manager; the clue splits his name into S (south) and a gate, a way in.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier posted to keep watch at a gate is a guard.

clue.text: Her plans could be fragmentary and dangerous

definitions.note: an adjective phrase describing the bomb fragments the noun names

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of her plans can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Her schemes might fall to pieces and be risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal fragments thrown out by an exploding shell are broken pieces that can kill.
